dispositionRules.why: PR 509 (merged as 7de5dc40): the name carries the creating pid and namespace, and a sweep at the start of the next run removes the dead owners' directories.

Chrome makes this directory itself; its name carries no owner. PR 515 removes it when the launching process survives to run its cleanup; a SIGKILLed runner runs none. It can be removed only through the profile's SingletonSocket link (follow-up F1).

Proposed, not covered by PR 509 or 515: name the profile with the owner pid and extend the sweep to it, reading SingletonSocket and refusing while a process still carries the --user-data-dir marker (follow-up F1). Until then a residual.

Created by vitest itself in its main process (TestProject.tmpDir = join(tmpdir(), nanoid())), before any test runs, so a test-kit root cannot contain it. A run wrapper that sets TMPDIR to an owner-pid root would (follow-up F3).
Created by npx/npm (module.enableCompileCache), one directory reused by every run, not one per run. Not growing; outside this repository.

Created by a non-test module under apps/ or packages/: operator code that a test runs (dossier-trigger.ts, self-corpus.ts) or test support (test-model-fixture.ts, cdp-browser.ts when no sweep applies). It calls os.tmpdir() at the point of use, which reads TMPDIR then, so a test-kit root installed as TMPDIR in the worker reaches it; the same code run by an operator keeps its directories in the operator's TMPDIR by design.

A lock file named for the uid and the port, made with O_EXCL by restart.ts (no trace line: the tracer does not wrap open). The code states its intent: "A stale lock requires operator inspection; the script never guesses that it is safe to remove one." A pid-based sweep would contradict that sentence, so no sweep is proposed; the stale lock matters only to a later run on the same port.
Unknown: no trace line carries the name and no shape rule names it, or the creating call has no frame under the repository root (third-party or Node internals). Not attributed to any file here.
Created by a test file. The kit's tempDir() (syzygy-bpyt.4.4) makes one owner-pid root per process and every test directory lives under it, so one sweep covers all of them.

staticGrepScope: git grep -F -l for the quoted stem (' " or `) in blobs of the commit under apps, packages, scripts and .syzygy, files ending .ts .mts .cts .js .mjs .cjs .py .sh; docs/ is left out because its evidence tools quote prefixes without creating them

exposureRanking.meaning: expected number of directories of the class present at a uniformly random moment of the clean run (sampler interval 0.5 s); the upper bound counts every name once for a whole sampler interval more than it was seen

finding: [Observed] A SIGKILL of the full run leaves 16 / 34 / 15 entries in the private temp directory (192.3 / 141.7 / 65.4 MB) at 40.0 / 75.0 / 115.0 s into the run, in 27 classes in all; 10 / 26 / 8 Chrome processes survive the kill of the process group, found by the --user-data-dir marker and stopped by pid.

[Observed] One fresh full run started in each kill's leftovers removed 1 / 10 / 4 of 16 / 34 / 15 entries, all of them of the two classes PR 509 sweeps (syzygy-poc-surface-fixture-p<pid>-n<ns>-, syzygy-poc-surface-fixture-template-p<pid>-n<ns>-); the other 15 / 24 / 11 stayed, in 25 classes.

[Observed] The seven runs together put 176 classes of entries directly in the temp directory (170 by mkdtemp): 163 by test files, 6 by non-test modules, 1 by cdp-browser.ts (the browser profile), 3 by Chrome, vitest and npm themselves, and 1 lock file made by restart.ts.

[Observed] The clean run itself leaves 2 entries (chrome-singleton-directory, node-compile-cache); this tree has no PR 515, so a clean run leaves Chrome singleton directories (3 / 1 / 3 in the fresh runs).

[Inferred] Which classes a given SIGKILL catches depends on what is alive at that moment. The expected number of directories of a class present at a random moment of the clean run is in exposureInTheCleanRun; the prefixes the bead observation names that none of these three kills left (syzygy-dossier-src-, syzygy-poc-surface-state-, syzygy-public-screen-, syzygy-trigger-, syzygy-trigger-repo-) have an upper bound of 0.156 or less, so a kill misses them most of the time and catches them sometimes.

followUps.title: Name the browser profile for its owner and sweep it with its Chrome directory and its orphan processes
followUps.size: small in code (one creating file, cdp-browser.ts), not trivially safe
followUps.what: Extend the PR 509 pattern to the syzygy-poc-browser- profile: the owner pid and namespace in its name; a sweep that removes it only when the owner is dead in this namespace, reads the profile's SingletonSocket link to remove the Chrome singleton directory under PR 515's guard, and first stops processes whose arguments carry --user-data-dir=<that profile>/ (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a wait: a stopped process ignores SIGTERM, seen once in an earlier set of these runs at a discarded commit, not retained).
followUps.whyNotTriviallySafe: It deletes recursively and signals processes by argument match; it needs an independent review and shares cdp-browser.ts with PR 515 (open).
followUps.measure: census_run.py kill run then --seed-tmp-from fresh run: classes syzygy-poc-browser- and chrome-singleton-directory must read stillThere 0 and the marker count 0.

followUps.title: Add a census acceptance criterion to syzygy-bpyt.4.4 (test-kit temp root)
followUps.size: a comment on an existing bead, no new bead
followUps.what: After a SIGKILLed full run and one fresh run in the same private TMPDIR, no entry remains except the classes of rules R2, R4, R5 and R7. A mechanism that reaches non-test modules too: the worker setup file assigns process.env.TMPDIR to an owner-pid root, because os.tmpdir() reads TMPDIR at each call. Budget: Chrome's socket path limits TMPDIR to 65 bytes (PR 515); the root adds about 40.
followUps.measure: the same runs: assemble_census.py leftBySIGKILL lists only R2, R4, R5, R7 classes after the fresh run.

followUps.title: Option, not proposed as small: a run wrapper that gives the whole vitest run an owner-pid TMPDIR
followUps.size: medium; changes how npm test is run (root manifest)
followUps.what: Children inherit TMPDIR, so vitest's project directories, npm's compile cache, Chrome's singleton directories and the restart lock would all land in one root swept by one rule. Costs: npm's compile cache stops being shared between runs; the 65-byte Chrome budget; the restart lock's by-design stale-lock behaviour is then moot only for killed runs. An owner or coordinator choice.

followUps.title: No sweep is proposed for the restart lock
followUps.what: restart.ts says "A stale lock requires operator inspection; the script never guesses that it is safe to remove one." The lock is named for the uid and the port, not a pid.

limits: The tracer wraps mkdtemp, mkdir, writeFile and symlink only (sync, callback and promise forms). A name made by open/openSync, copyFile, rename, link, cp, a stream, or by a process that is not Node has no trace line: it is classed by shape, or by the static stem and labelled inferred.
The sampler lists the temp directory every 0.5 s. A directory that lives less than that can be missed; the exposure bounds say so.

Three SIGKILL points (about 25, 50 and 75 percent of a clean run of about 150 s) catch the directories alive at that moment. A class absent from every kill is not thereby safe; its disposition rests on its creating file, not on a leftover.
The root vitest run only. test:system (packages/cap1-system) and the Python and shell scripts are in the static census, not in any run.
Runs shared the host with other work (load average at each start is recorded); one fresh run exited 1 on two 5000 ms test timeouts.

The fresh run after each kill starts in that kill's leftovers renamed into a new private temp directory; the process ids of the dead owners are not reused within the minutes between the runs [Inferred].
